Alex.confusing: How Kookaburra confusion and hugs interact with claims; it was hard to tell wrong reports from lies.
Alex.fun: Round 2: my Kookaburra visit revealed Blair as the Sphinx, and the table converged on Blair right away.
Alex.change: Make the score gap smaller. Big stakes on a sure Meowfia let one player pull far ahead, and Farm won every round, so the game felt lopsided.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw only 4, 4 and a Wild at Casey. I should have kept the Wilds, which were worth nothing, and thrown less. In round 1 I also made an unverified claim that Blair's Eagle story was off, then retracted it. I would have kept the focus on Casey.

Blair.confusing: How Meowfia stakes score: they only bank if the target is the Farm player who gets eggsecuted. That made throwing as Meowfia feel pointless when the team was already losing.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when my Hawk egg confirmed Casey was Meowfia and the table converged on her. Banking 29 points from my three-card throw was satisfying.
Blair.change: I'd make the Meowfia's safe-claim info more useful. The not-in-play animal was their only edge, and Farm players could expose it by cross-checking visitors.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I claimed Turkey and said nobody visited me, but three players had visited me, so the lie was easy to catch. I should have deflected toward someone else, or claimed a role that needed no visitors to check out.

Casey.confusing: How the Turkey claim interacts with visitors and hugs, and why nest sizes and scores swing so much between rounds; the final score scale (pile values of 76 vs my 0) was also surprising.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when the table converged on Blair and my fake Falcon claim held up unchallenged.
Casey.change: Give Meowfia a safer way to score, since being on the losing team three rounds in a row left me with no banked cards at all.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I claimed Turkey, which a Turkey's visitor eggs contradicted, and then I never staked any cards. I should have claimed a role I could cover, and in rounds 2 and 3 I should have thrown high cards at the player the table was targeting to bank something.

Drew.confusing: How the Kookaburra's confusion worked: in round 3 my report named Casey as Tit, and I couldn't tell whether that was true or a scrambled result.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when several players' claims lined up against Blair's false Turkey story and we got a clean Farm win.
Drew.change: Show the standings, or at least the score piles, sooner, so players can judge who is ahead. As it was, I couldn't tell I was trailing Finley.
Drew.regret: I threw all my high cards every round to bank points and never thought about Finley running away with the lead. Finley won with 95. I should have tracked the standings and thrown at different targets or stakes to catch up, since only first place counts.

Ellis.confusing: How the Meowfia stake works: it only banks at 2x if you hit the Farm player who gets eggsecuted. It was also unclear who the winker was and why Blair was killed.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, where my Falcon result (Alex visited Casey) helped break Casey's fake Turkey claim and the table converged on a Meowfia.
Ellis.change: Give Meowfia more ways to coordinate. As Meowfia I had almost no way to influence the vote, and I picked my hug target at random.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw a Wild at my partner Casey, which made me look like part of the pile-on and did nothing for my side. I should have thrown at Finley, the loudest Farm voice, and pushed doubt on his too-perfect Eagle story to split the vote.

Finley.confusing: Nothing major. The one unclear point was whether the pool announcement applied every round, because players kept disputing which animals were in play.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when my Eagle report of Casey's three visitors matched Drew, Alex and Blair exactly. Then Blair was winked right after naming Casey, which made the Meowfia easy to read.
Finley.change: I'd give Farm roles more ways to confirm each other, because the Eagle and Falcon cross-checks decided every round. Winks could also leave some trace, since a silent kill is hard to answer.
Finley.regret: None. In round 1 I guessed Mouser on Alex with no information, and a better guess would have been a cheap improvement. The outcome was still fine.

review.title: Three Easy Hangings
review.headline: Three rounds, three obvious cats hanged, and Finley's lucky Kings won it.
review.summary: Each round the table converged on one Meowfia and eggsecuted them. Casey's wink and clumsy Turkey claim lost round 1. Blair's Sphinx was exposed by Alex's Kookaburra in round 2. In round 3 Finley's Eagle drew three eggs, including two 13s, and he banked them for a runaway win. The second cat was never hunted, because the first was always caught.

rounds.recap: Casey claimed Turkey but Drew, Alex and Ellis had all visited her, so the lie was obvious. Casey winked Alex to cut a vote, but it was too late and everyone threw at her. Blair, her partner, hid and threw a cheap card at Drew.

Blair claimed Turkey, but Finley, Drew and Alex had all visited him, and Alex's Kookaburra learned he was the Sphinx. Everyone piled on Blair. Casey's Falcon claim was shaky and Blair's challenge to it was dismissed. Casey threw nothing.

Blair's Hawk egg pointed at Casey, and Finley's Eagle report matched the three visitors. Casey winked Blair, which confirmed a Mouser existed. Casey was eggsecuted. Ellis threw a Wild and stayed unseen, but his team still lost. Finley's +3 eggs of top cards made him the winner.

highlights.text: Casey winks Alex right as the CAW ends the day, a desperate move that gave away that a Mouser existed.
Alex's Kookaburra reveals Blair is the Sphinx, ending Blair's fake Turkey claim on the spot.
Finley's Eagle visits Casey and learns the exact three visitors, which matched Drew, Alex and Blair's claims.
Finley receives three eggs (H7, H13, D13) from an unrelated source and ends with 95 points.

confusions.what: Said Falcon was not in the pool, though it was listed. The claim was wrong.
Argued a Turkey would have given Drew an egg, but Drew was hugged and an Eagle's no-visitors claim was also misjudged. Alex retracted part of it.
Threw her three highest cards at Casey with confidence. This was fine but she was winked and still threw, which is correct.
Said Casey had visitors, which is true but did not recognize that Turkey would have given eggs to Alex too.

worked: Egg counts as evidence: a Turkey claim with visitors, or a Hawk egg, gave clean, checkable deductions.
Kookaburra's role learn in round 2 gave one decisive, clear piece of information.
Wink as a desperate move: it created doubt in round 3 and exposed the Mouser.
problems: Meowfia almost always claim Turkey or Falcon with no cover story, and they lost every round. Give cats a safer lie, such as telling them which Farm animals actually visited whom.
The Meowfia never won a round. The second cat was never suspected, so the vote is a trivial pile-on. Consider a cost to a unanimous pile-on, or a stronger way for cats to inject doubt.
Stakes favour a runaway: Finley's three free eggs, including two 13s, decided the game. An Eagle that draws one egg per visitor is too swingy. Cap it or reduce it.
Scores are lopsided after round 1 (Blair and Casey at 5-7), so players on the losing team are out of the race. Add catch-up so third rounds stay in doubt.
Wink is nearly useless: Casey's winks only killed a talker and did not save her. A silent wink could change outcomes, but it needs a better design.
